scope: SQLite official pragma.html, limits.html and lang_explain.html; defaults and timings are version- and platform-dependent

claims.claim: PRAGMA cache_size is a suggestion of the maximum number of pages held in memory; the built-in default is -2000 (about 2MB), and a negative N means KiB rather than pages (behavior of negative N changed in 3.7.10)
claims.notes: Replaces the earlier chapter's invented pagerFixCache() LRU description

claims.claim: PRAGMA synchronous accepts OFF(0)/NORMAL(1)/FULL(2)/EXTRA(3); NORMAL syncs less often, is corruption-safe in WAL mode but can lose a committed transaction after power loss
PRAGMA mmap_size sets the maximum number of bytes for memory-mapped I/O on a database
PRAGMA temp_store accepts DEFAULT(0)/FILE(1)/MEMORY(2) and controls where temporary tables and indices are stored
PRAGMA page_size must be a power of two between 512 and 65536 and is assigned when the database is created
A database may have at most 4294967294 pages; at the maximum 65536-byte page size that is about 281 TB, and this upper bound is untested by the developers
claims.notes: Corrects the earlier chapter's 140TB figure, which only holds at a smaller page size

claims.claim: EXPLAIN outputs the VDBE instruction listing for a prepared statement while EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN outputs a higher-level description of the strategy; the CLI .eqp toggles automatic query-plan output
claims.notes: Earlier chapter's fixed opcode/address listing removed; exact opcodes are version-dependent

claims.claim: Wrapping many INSERTs in a single transaction avoids per-statement commit work (such as disk synchronization), which is the main reason batched inserts are much faster
claims.notes: Mechanistic explanation; the earlier chapter's 30s->0.5s story and 10-100x figures were removed as unverifiable
